description: The pie chart represents the distribution of samples across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity. The chart is divided into two concentric rings, with the outer ring representing the ambiguity standard deviation and the inner ring representing the maximum ambiguity. The outer ring is divided into four segments, with the largest segment representing a standard deviation of 0.82, followed by a segment representing a standard deviation of 0.47, a segment representing a standard deviation of 0.94, and the smallest segment representing a standard deviation of 0.0. The inner ring is divided into three segments, with the largest segment representing a maximum ambiguity of 2, followed by a segment representing a maximum ambiguity of 1, and the smallest segment representing a maximum ambiguity of 3. The chart does not include any percentage labels inside the slices or any visual emphasis on any slices. The segments are ordered in descending size, with the largest segment representing a standard deviation of 0.82 and a maximum ambiguity of 2.
